questions.prompt: The cook cooked the meat which the hunter had carried home.
questions.answer: Coquus carnem coxit quam vēnātor domum vexerat.

questions.prompt: Having covered the fields with snow, winter oppressed the farmers.
questions.answer: Hiems, agrīs nive tēctīs, agricolās oppressit.

questions.prompt: The silent slave crept through the dark garden.
questions.answer: Servus tacitus per hortum obscūrum rēpsit.

questions.prompt: The waves had shattered the ship which the sailors had joined with ropes.
questions.answer: Flūctūs nāvem afflīxerant quam nautae fūnibus iūnxerant.

questions.prompt: The old woman, having plucked the flowers, made garlands.
questions.answer: Anus, flōribus carptīs, corōnās fēcit.

questions.prompt: The enemy, whom fear had drawn into flight, threw away their weapons.
questions.answer: Hostēs, quōs metus in fugam trāxerat, arma ēiēcērunt.

questions.prompt: The priest anointed the altar and then dipped the branch in wine.
questions.answer: Sacerdōs āram ūnxit et deinde rāmum vīnō tīnxit.

questions.prompt: The messenger, sent by the king, wrote down everything the king had said.
questions.answer: Nūntius, ā rēge missus, omnia quae rēx dīxerat scrīpsit.

questions.prompt: The horses, joined to the chariot, drew the victor through the streets.
questions.answer: Equī, carrō iūnctī, victōrem per viās trāxērunt.

questions.prompt: The woman married a wealthy husband although her father had despised him.
questions.answer: Mulier marītō dīvitī nūpsit quamquam pater eum contempserat.

questions.prompt: The serpent crawled across the threshold while everyone slept.
questions.answer: Serpēns trāns līmen serpsit dum omnēs dormiunt.

questions.prompt: The artist, having painted the queen, chiselled her likeness in marble.
questions.answer: Artifex, rēgīnā pīctā, effigiem eius in marmore sculpsit.

questions.prompt: The commander covered the wounded with cloaks and led them to safety.
questions.answer: Dux vulnerātōs sagīs tēxit et in tūtum dūxit.

questions.prompt: The farmer had plucked the ripe grapes and cooked sweet wine.
questions.answer: Agricola ūvās mātūrās carpserat et dulce vīnum coxerat.

questions.prompt: The painter had painted a swan on the wall of the temple.
questions.answer: Pictor cycnum in pariete dēlūbrī pīnxerat.

questions.prompt: The wise king, having conquered his enemies, ruled the city justly.
questions.answer: Rēx sapiēns, hostibus superātīs, urbem iūstē rēxit.

questions.prompt: The general led the swift soldiers across the river at first light.
questions.answer: Dux mīlitēs celerēs prīmā lūce trāns flūmen dūxit.

questions.prompt: The oxen drew the heavy wagon which the farmer had filled with grain.
questions.answer: Bovēs plaustrum grave, quod agricola frūmentō complēverat, trāxērunt.

questions.prompt: The snow covered the fields which the rustic farmers had plowed.
questions.answer: Nix agrōs, quōs rusticī agricolae arāverant, tēxit.

questions.prompt: The soldiers girded the walls of the city with a strong rampart.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs mūrōs urbis firmō vāllō cīnxērunt.

questions.prompt: For many years the Romans waged a dreadful war against the Gauls.
questions.answer: Multōs annōs Rōmānī bellum horrendum contrā Gallōs gessērunt.
